chunks: Muhammad ibn Ishaq at-Taliqani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narrated from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said:
He who denies the Mi'raj (Night Ascension) has indeed denied the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).

key_terms.بِالْمِعْرَاجِ: The Night Ascension (Mi'raj), the journey of the Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Jerusalem and through the heavens.
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
key_terms.ع: Abbreviation for 'Alayhi al-Salam' (peace be upon him), used for the Imams.

ai.seo_question: What is the theological consequence of denying the Mi'raj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Sifat al-Shia*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Rida (as) linking the denial of the Mi'raj directly to the denial of the Prophet’s truthfulness, thereby elevating it from a miraculous event to a core tenet of faith. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Mi'raj is a definitive, historical reality confirmed by the Quran, making its rejection tantamount to rejecting the prophetic mission itself.

en.badr-shahin: Muhammed b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq at-Taliqani (rah) narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammed b. Sa'eed al-Hamadani from Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Fadhal from his father that Abul Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Ridha (as) said:
He who denies the Midnight Ascension is belying Rasulullah (s).
